description:
Project Overview

This is a fully funded PhD studentship in the research group of Dr Maya Al-Sid-Cheikh (School of Chemistry), examining the environmental and health impacts of titanium dioxide (TiO2) and toxic metal exposures in communities near mining operations.

Research Focus

  • Exposure Characterization: Quantifying TiO2-bearing and metal particulates in air
  • Isotopic Fingerprinting: Using multi-collector ICP-MS/ICP-QQQ-MS/SP-ICPMS
  • Dispersion Mapping: Using isoscape/ISOSCAPE-style framework
  • Toxicological Assessment: Evaluating oxidative stress/inflammation pathways
  • Epidemiology: Exploring associations between exposure and health outcomes

Funding & Benefits

  • Tuition Fees: Full coverage for 42 months
  • Stipend: £21,805 per year (UKRI rate 2026-27) for 42 months
  • Research Costs: Access to analytical facilities and fieldwork
  • Training: Comprehensive training in analytical methods

Eligibility Criteria

  • Strong MSc degree (or undergraduate with minimum 2:1 grade)
  • Field: Analytical chemistry, geochemistry, environmental chemistry
  • Interest in ecotoxicology and public health
  • Laboratory experience in analytical chemistry
  • Residency: Open to UK students satisfying EPSRC residency criteria

Application Process

  1. Complete EDI Form (School of Chemistry Equality, Diversity & Inclusion Form)
  2. Submit application by email including cover letter and CV
  3. Provide transcripts and three referees
  4. Review and shortlisting
  5. Interview process

Required Documents

  • Cover Letter (max 2 pages)
  • CV (max 3 pages) including technical skills section
  • Academic Transcripts (unofficial acceptable at first stage)
  • Three Referees with contact details and relationship description
  • EDI Form Receipt Number
